remarks: No active tropical cyclones in the JMA basin for a fifth straight run. Nothing is bearing down on any tracked port and no threat rows are scored this run.

No tracked port is suspended. The only operations-stopping events this week hit ports the tracker does not follow: gale-force winds closed Dalian for 32 hours and Lianyungang for 14.5 hours, both since reopened.

Shanghai/Ningbo is the one tracked port with a live entry, and the reason has changed. The storm story is over; the current disruption is seasonal fishing traffic closing the navigation channels, on top of a backlog that has not cleared.

Qingdao, Yantian, Busan and Singapore are all open and omitted. Yantian berth delays of 2-3 days for mega-vessels and Busan yard density near 90% are peak-season congestion, not weather, so the congestion panel is the right place to read them.

Busan terminals will halt for 24 hours from 25 to 26 September for Chuseok. Noted here rather than as a port entry because it is a scheduled holiday, not a disruption, and it would expire off the page long before it happens.

Linerlytica has not published a congestion snapshot since 6 September, so the congestion panel is now five days behind. congestion.json was left untouched again this run rather than rewritten with no new data.
